title: FOMO and chasing
desc: Why buying the spike costs you, and what to do instead

cards.title: Everyone’s buying
cards.situation: A stock jumps 15% in an hour on one big green candle. Everyone online is buying. You have no setup. What’s the main risk of buying now?

chart.label: Five flat hourly candles near $100, then one big green candle to $115

options.text: None: the move will keep going
options.feedback: Big moves often pull back. At the top of a spike, there’s nowhere sensible for a stop.

options.text: You buy high, with no clear stop
options.feedback: Late buyers pay the highest price and carry the most risk.

options.text: You’re too late to make anything
options.feedback: It might keep going, so “too late” isn’t the problem. Buying at the top of a spike leaves nowhere sensible for a stop.

cards.work: Bought at $115 after a run from $100. A dip to $107 = −$8 a share, over half the move.

cards.title: FOMO: fear of missing out
cards.text: **[[fomo|FOMO]]** is the itch to jump in because a price is flying and everyone else is in. It makes you buy **after** the move, not before it.

chart.label: A spike to $115, then red candles back toward $109

blocks.tip: If you missed it, you missed it. Another setup always comes.

cards.title: Chase or wait?
cards.text: Two traders see the same spike.

chart.label: Bought at $115 on the spike; price falls back to about $107
Waits for the pullback: buy at $108 with a stop at $105

blocks.tip: The waiter knows where he’s wrong. The chaser is just hoping.

cards.title: Popular isn’t a plan
cards.text: By the time a stock is all over social media, much of the move has usually happened. The crowd tends to arrive last.

items.title: Your setup, entry, stop and target
items.sub: A plan you wrote before the move.

cards.title: You missed the breakout
cards.q: Your plan: buy at $50, stop at $48. You missed it. Now it’s $56 and rising. What should you do?

options.feedback: Most people feel that urge. Chasing changes the trade: same stop, four times the risk.

options.text: Skip it, or wait for a pullback
options.feedback: Your plan only worked near $50. Letting it go, or waiting for a pullback, keeps the risk you planned.

options.text: Buy double to make up for missing it
options.feedback: Double size at a worse price is FOMO and revenge at once: eight times the risk you planned.
“Too high” isn’t a setup. Shorting a rising stock with no plan is just a different chase.

cards.work: Planned: $50 − $48 = $2 a share. Now: $56 − $48 = $8 a share.

cards.title: Beat the FOMO
cards.q: What’s the best fix for FOMO?

options.text: Trade every big move so you never miss out
options.feedback: Chasing every big move means buying late, again and again. That’s FOMO as a strategy.

options.text: Write your setup down and enter only when it shows
options.feedback: A written setup tells you when to act, and when to sit out.
Easy to fall for: trending stocks are where FOMO is loudest. A written setup tells you when to act, and when to sit out.

options.text: Use bigger size on hot stocks
options.feedback: Bigger size on a hot stock makes the chase more expensive when it pulls back.

cards.headline: You can let a move go without chasing it.
lines: FOMO makes you buy after the move, near the top.
Chasing raises your risk with the same stop.
No setup, no trade. Another one always comes.
